Stone Abilities

Stone Abilities

Stones are a player-facing measure of your awakened potential. In the fiction, they represent inner strength, not physical objects. A warrior aligned with Might unleashes raw destruction; a rogue aligned with Agility moves like a blur of shadows; a mage aligned with Intellect overloads the arcane weave.

Attributes and Stones are intentionally independent. Attribute values determine dice Pools. Lifetime Experience determines how many permanent Stones you earn.

The Core Chain

  • Characters begin with 2 permanent Attribute Stones. Both must be assigned to Attributes; neither starting Stone may be Colorless.
  • Every 20 Lifetime XP grants 1 additional permanent Stone.
  • Stones earned after the 2 starting Stones may be assigned to any Attribute or chosen as Permanent Colorless Stones during an Upgrade Step. Each such permanent Stone grants exactly 1 Attribute Stone or 1 Permanent Colorless Stone. Unassigned Stones cannot be spent.
  • Choosing a Permanent Colorless Stone costs no additional Stones (1:1). The choice is permanent. The 2 starting Stones are always Attribute Stones and cannot later be converted to Colorless.
  • The first Stone assigned to an Attribute creates that Attribute's Stone Pool and ordinarily unlocks 8 Stone Abilities:
    • 4 General Stone Abilities (same for all Attributes)
    • 4 Attribute Stone Abilities (unique to that Attribute)
  • A single Attribute may hold at most Mastery Rank × 2 permanent Stones.
  • There is no separate Mastery Rank cap on Permanent Colorless Stones; a character may choose every permanent Stone earned after the 2 starting Stones as Colorless.
  • Permanent Colorless Stones are not assigned to an Attribute and do not count against any Attribute Stone limit. They may pay the normal cost of any unlocked Stone Ability unless a rule explicitly excludes Colorless Stones. Only an Attribute Stone unlocks that Attribute's Stone Abilities; Colorless Stones alone do not unlock them.
  • Once a Stone is assigned or converted into a Permanent Colorless Stone, that choice remains unless a rule explicitly allows it to change.

In short: Attributes define capability. Stones define supernatural affinity. Colorless Stones trade normal recoverability for flexibility.

Stone States

Stones exist in 4 states:

  • Ready: available to be used.
  • Exhausted: spent during the current combat flow. Attribute Stones can return through Stone Recovery. Colorless Stones are not recoverable unless selected by Influence Stone Ability: Colorless Recovery.
  • Sealed: locked by Rituals or an Ability that explicitly Seals Stones (such as Remove Scar); cannot recover at the end of a Round and returns only after a Safe Haven Rest.
  • Bound: Permanently invested (Artifacts, Familiars, Summons, etc.). Bound Stones are not part of your usable pool and do not recover. They return to your Stone Pool only when the bond is broken or the investment is released.

Colorless Stones

Every permanent Stone earned after the 2 starting Attribute Stones may be chosen as a Permanent Colorless Stone at a 1:1 ratio, with no MR-based cap. The 2 starting Attribute Stones cannot be converted to Colorless later. Colorless Stones can pay the normal costs of any eligible unlocked Stone Ability, but do not unlock Attribute Stone Abilities themselves. Their source determines when they are gained, when they expire, and any explicit source-specific restrictions.

One recovery rule for all Colorless Stones: Spent Colorless Stones become Exhausted. They cannot be restored through normal Stone Recovery by default, regardless of source. Influence Stone Ability: Colorless Recovery is the way to make up to 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 Colorless Stones eligible for the existing shared Stone Recovery limit (Ranks 1–4; normal activation costs 1 / 3 / 7 / 15 Stones). This Ability is activated once per combat at one chosen Rank; its designation lasts until combat ends. The activation Stones become Exhausted, not Sealed, and may be recovered according to their normal rules. It cannot be activated again or upgraded during the same combat. This does not grant Stones or increase the MR Stones per Round Recovery rate. The designation changes eligibility for recovery, not the Stone's Ready/Exhausted state.

  • Permanent Colorless Stones persist between combats. Unrecovered Exhausted permanent Colorless Stones become Ready at end of combat, like other permanent Stones, unless Sealed or Bound.
  • Initiative Colorless Stones are gained Ready through Initiative Exchange and last until end of combat, whether Ready or Exhausted. They do not count as permanent progression or affect MR and cannot be Burned, Sealed, or Bound.
  • Absorption Colorless Stones are earned when eligible hostile damage causes a Health Bar to become Scarred while Passive: Absorption is slotted. Each such Health Bar uses one of at most four Absorption triggers per combat; the Passive grants 1–8 Stones per trigger by Power Level. The earned Stones become Ready in the next Preparation Phase. They expire at end of combat; no HP-loss remainder is tracked.
  • Other granted Colorless Stones follow the creation and expiration conditions of their source. They are not recoverable by default, but may be selected by Colorless Recovery while they exist; that Ability never extends their original duration. Any source-specific restriction on spending, Sealing, Binding, or Burning still applies.

All Colorless Stones share the same spending Pool. Source distinctions affect persistence and any explicit source-specific restrictions, not ordinary recovery eligibility.

Spending Stones

During the Preparation Phase at the start of each Round, first receive any Absorption Colorless Stones earned since your previous Preparation Phase. Those Stones are Ready and may be used when you choose and commit Stone Abilities for this Round. You may spend any number of Ready Stones available to you across your Stone Abilities, but no Stone Ability can ever be raised beyond Rank 4. Attribute Stones, Permanent Colorless Stones, Initiative Colorless Stones, and Absorption Colorless Stones may be used where their rules allow. When spent, an Attribute Stone or Colorless Stone becomes Exhausted unless a specific effect explicitly removes that Stone. Spent Colorless Stones remain unavailable through normal Stone Recovery unless designated by Influence: Colorless Recovery; temporary Stones still expire when their source says they expire. Once the first Turn of the Round begins, your Stone choices for that Round are locked unless a rule explicitly allows a change. Stone Abilities with a specific Turn timing or trigger are still prepared during the Preparation Phase, but their effect resolves only when that timing or trigger occurs.

Round-Based Stone Ability Duration

Round-based Stone Abilities are prepared and paid for during the Preparation Phase before the Round begins. Their effects become available immediately, unless the Ability specifies a later resolution timing or trigger. A Round-based Stone Ability remains available for the entire current Round, independently of the activating character's Turn or Initiative position. Any unused Round-based benefits expire at the end of that Round, before the next Preparation Phase begins. Round-based effects never carry over into the next Round. A character must prepare and pay for the Ability again during the next Preparation Phase to receive its benefits again. Abilities that explicitly provide a longer duration, a once-per-combat allowance, or a lasting result follow their specific rules instead.

All Stone Abilities have 4 Ranks. They use one of two cost progressions.

Normal Stone Abilities

Rank Additional Cost Total Cost
Rank 1 1 Stone 1 Stone
Rank 2 2 Stones 3 Stones
Rank 3 4 Stones 7 Stones
Rank 4 8 Stones 15 Stones

Premium Stone Abilities

Rank Additional Cost Total Cost
Rank 1 2 Stones 2 Stones
Rank 2 4 Stones 6 Stones
Rank 3 6 Stones 12 Stones
Rank 4 8 Stones 20 Stones

The following are Premium Stone Abilities: Extra Attack, Parry, Crit, Damage Negation, Special Boost, Damage Reduction, Not a Target, and Phasing. All other Stone Abilities use the Normal cost progression.

Rank 4 is the absolute maximum. There are no higher Stone Ability Ranks. A Premium Rank 4 may exceed the normal Stone capacity of one Attribute and can therefore require Colorless Stones, Stone Power Support, or another rule that explicitly provides usable Stones.

Stone Power Support

Stone Power Support pre-fills one named Rank of a Stone Ability. The supported Rank costs no Stones from the character, but every lower Rank required to reach it must still be activated and paid normally. Support never skips unpaid lower Ranks.

  • Support for Rank 2 requires Rank 1 to be paid normally.
  • Support for Rank 3 requires Ranks 1 and 2 to be paid normally.
  • Support for Rank 4 requires Ranks 1, 2, and 3 to be paid normally.

Vitality: Maximization Support follows this rule without adding charges of its own. Rank 2 / 3 / 4 Support pre-fills the corresponding 2 / 4 / 8 Stone incremental cost. The character still pays lower required Ranks (1 / 3 / 7 Stones for supported Rank 2 / 3 / 4) during the first Preparation Phase of combat. The resulting allowance remains 2 / 3 / 4 shared Maximization uses for Damage or Healing Rolls during that combat, not a second or recurring activation. Support can be used with a Limited Power, including the Hunter's Scourge Limited Strike, if its other requirements are met.

Stone Ability costs reset each Preparation Phase unless an Ability explicitly states that its cost is cumulative per combat.

Stone Recovery

  • At the end of each Round, recover a total number of Exhausted Stones equal to your Mastery Rank.
  • Choose those Stones freely from your Attribute Stone Pools and Colorless Stones designated by Influence: Colorless Recovery, irrespective of whether the Colorless Stones were Permanent, gained from Initiative Exchange, generated by Absorption, or granted by another effect.
  • This is one shared limit of MR recovered Stones per Round. Colorless Recovery grants neither additional Stones nor additional recovery.
  • Spent Colorless Stones not designated by Colorless Recovery remain Exhausted and cannot return through normal Stone Recovery. Temporary Colorless Stones disappear when their source duration ends; Exhausted permanent Colorless Stones return Ready at end of combat. Sealed / Bound Stones cannot be returned through this recovery.

General Stone Abilities

Stone Ability Rank 1 Rank 2 Rank 3 Rank 4
Extra Attack +1 Attack Action +2 Attack Actions +3 Attack Actions +4 Attack Actions
Extra Movement +1 Movement +2 Movements +3 Movements +4 Movements
Extra Reaction +1 Reaction +2 Reactions +3 Reactions +4 Reactions
Movement Enhancement +4 m per Movement +8 m per Movement +12 m per Movement +16 m per Movement

Round duration. Unless expressly stated otherwise, Stone Abilities are prepared and paid for in the Preparation Phase. Round-based effects apply throughout the upcoming Round and end at Round End, not at the start of the user's next Turn. Triggered effects resolve at their stated timing. Combat-long allowances and lasting results follow their own rules.

Movement Enhancement. Add the listed distance once to each Movement Action this Round, including normal Move, Dash, Disengage, eligible Movement Powers, and Extra Movements. Calculate the normal distance first (including Dash doubling), then add the bonus before applying distance reductions and rounding. This grants no extra Action or movement mode, changes no base Speed, bypasses no Root, Immovable, or terrain restriction, and does not affect Quick Load or Passive swapping. Normal Stone costs: 1 / 3 / 7 / 15.

Additional Attack Action Limit. Extra Attack Actions from different sources do not stack unless explicitly allowed; use the highest single grant. Stone Power Support modifies the same Extra Attack activation, not a separate source. Your normal Attack Action remains available.

Temporary Defensive Stone Values

Stone bonuses to existing defenses add to their corresponding values under the normal rules. A Stone Ability can provide Parry, Damage Negation, Damage Reduction, or Special Negation even without a previously learned source. All Round-based defensive Stone bonuses expire at Round End.

Damage Negation is a single expendable pool for the current Round, not a fresh allowance per attack. Before a Damage Roll, spend any number of its remaining points; each point removes 1 Damage Die. You may divide the pool among multiple incoming attacks. Spend temporary Negation before the Passive's combat reserve. Unused temporary points expire at Round End.

Might Stone Abilities

Stone Ability Rank 1 Rank 2 Rank 3 Rank 4
Parry +2 Parry Pool +4 Parry Pool +6 Parry Pool +8 Parry Pool
Damage +2 Damage Dice +4 Damage Dice +8 Damage Dice +16 Damage Dice
Armor +4 Armor +8 Armor +16 Armor +32 Armor
Armor Reduction Ignore 4 Armor Ignore 8 Armor Ignore 16 Armor Ignore 32 Armor

Parry / Armor. The bonus lasts for the current Round. Parry increases your existing Martial or Spell Parry Pool without changing its chosen delivery or making an ineligible effect parryable.

Damage. Add the indicated dice to your next damaging Martial Attack this Turn, whether melee, ranged, natural weapon, or Martial AoE. This does not increase Spell damage.

Armor Reduction. Applies to every damaging Attack you make this Round, including Martial and Spell Attacks. Only your own attacks ignore the listed Armor; the target's Armor against other attackers is unchanged. This combines with Corrode(X) and eligible Weapon Special: Penetration(X), but effective Armor cannot fall below 0. Penetration is not available as a generic Active or Active Buff.

Agility Stone Abilities

Stone Ability Rank 1 Rank 2 Rank 3 Rank 4
Crit 1 pool with Critical(1) 2 pools with Critical(1) 3 pools with Critical(1) 4 pools with Critical(1)
Evade +8 Evade +16 Evade +24 Evade +32 Evade
Safe Movement Move up to 4 m safely Move up to 8 m safely Move up to 12 m safely Move up to 16 m safely
Invisibility Boost +1 Invisibility Bonus +2 Invisibility Bonus +4 Invisibility Bonus +8 Invisibility Bonus

Crit. During the current Round, designate the listed number of Martial Attack Pools or damaging Spell Casting Pools. Choose each before its roll. Each chosen pool gains Critical(1): natural 7s and 8s explode.

Evade. The bonus lasts until Round End.

Safe Movement. The listed movement does not provoke movement-triggered Reactions; other normal movement restrictions still apply.

Invisibility Boost. Improves an existing Invisibility Bonus for the current Round and its related Perception TN. It does not grant Invisibility, change obscured Combat Senses, or block senses that could already detect the creature.

Vitality Stone Abilities

Stone Ability Rank 1 Rank 2 Rank 3 Rank 4
Damage Negation +2 Negation +4 Negation +8 Negation +12 Negation
Temporary HP 20 Temporary HP 40 Temporary HP 80 Temporary HP 160 Temporary HP
Maximization 1 use per combat 2 uses per combat 3 uses per combat 4 uses per combat
Remove Scar 1 Bar, Seal 1 Stone 1 Bar, Seal 2 Stones 1 Bar, Seal 4 Stones 1 Bar, Seal 8 Stones

Damage Negation. Premium costs: 2 / 6 / 12 / 20 Stones. Gain one expendable pool for the current Round. Each point removes 1 Damage Die before rolling; divide it among incoming attacks as needed. Unused points expire at Round End.

Temporary HP. Activate once per combat. The HP remain until depleted or combat ends, including across multiple hits. Spent Stones become Exhausted and may recover, but recovery does not permit a second activation. This differs from Reaction-granted Temporary HP, which protects one damage instance only.

Maximization

Activate once in the first Preparation Phase of combat. Pay 1 / 3 / 7 / 15 Stones (eligible Colorless Stones allowed); the Stones become Exhausted. Gain 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 shared uses for that combat. The Rank cannot change and unused uses expire at combat end.

Spend one use before an eligible complete Damage or Healing Roll: each d8 counts as 8, without triggering any natural-8 effect. For damage, apply Damage Negation first and maximize only the remaining dice, then resolve Armor and other mitigation. A complete roll includes eligible Weapon, Power, and Limited dice. Martial, Spell, Reaction, and Artifact damage qualify. One shared AoE roll uses one charge; separate rolls each use one. No targets, Range, AoE, or Action costs change.

For Healing, apply the current-Bar HP cap and the positive-Healing exception for living Incapacitated or Stable creatures. Resolve: Healing qualifies; Restoration has no Healing Roll. Damage Transfer heals only actual HP lost, even after Maximization of its Damage Roll.

Remove Scar

Each Rank restores 1 Scarred Health Bar and Seals its printed Vitality Stones. Cumulative totals through Ranks 1–4 are 1 / 3 / 7 / 15 Sealed Stones for up to 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 restored Bars. Activation is allowed outside combat. Ranks already used since the last Safe Haven Rest cannot be repeated; when advancing, pay and resolve only unused Ranks. Colorless Stones cannot pay. Sealed Stones return only after a Safe Haven Rest.

Artifact exception. The Artifact Level-10 Awakening's once-per-Safe-Haven-Rest cost-free supported activation pays and Seals 0 Stones, including prerequisite Ranks, and restores only still-unused Ranks. Ordinary Stone Power Support instead covers just its named Rank; lower Ranks must be paid and Sealed (e.g., Rank 4 Support leaves 7 Vitality Stones to pay for Ranks 1–3).

Intellect Stone Abilities

Stone Ability Rank 1 Rank 2 Rank 3 Rank 4
Raises 2 Free Raises 4 Free Raises 6 Free Raises 8 Free Raises
Range & AoE Boost +10 m Range, +2 m Reach, +1 m Radius +20 m, +4 m, +2 m +30 m, +6 m, +3 m +40 m, +8 m, +4 m
Special Boost +2 Special(X) +4 Special(X) +8 Special(X) +12 Special(X)
Spell Resistance +4 Spell Resistance +8 Spell Resistance +12 Spell Resistance +16 Spell Resistance

Raises. The listed Free Raises form one shared allowance for the current Round, usable on eligible rolls with any Attribute, including Martial and Spell rolls. Declare the number before rolling; choose permitted effects after a successful roll. Declared Free Raises are spent even on failure. They add no TN or Raise Cost; Paid Raises still add +4 TN each and have no Raise Cost. They cannot bypass a prohibition on Raises. Unused Free Raises expire at Round End.

Range & AoE Boost. During the current Round, improve only delivery components an eligible Attack or Power already possesses: Range, Melee Reach, and/or an existing AoE radius. This grants no new delivery mode, AoE, target, or attack. The temporary bonus may exceed the Power's purchased radius cap without changing its base profile.

Special Boost. A Premium Stone Ability. Each eligible numeric Special(X) you successfully deliver during the Round gains the listed bonus, including Martial, Spell, Weapon, Power, Artifact, Reaction, and applicable persistent effects. Add successful Raise increases first, then Special Boost, eligible Passive: Special Amplification for the owner's attack, and target Vulnerability; then apply Special Negation and the per-Round Special Application Limit. The Passive does not amplify persistent effects. No new, binary, or nonnumeric Special is created or improved.

Spell Resistance. Lasts until Round End and increases your Final Spell TN against both direct Spells and Spell AoEs that affect you.

Resolve Stone Abilities

Stone Ability Rank 1 Rank 2 Rank 3 Rank 4
Damage Reduction +10% DR +20% DR +30% DR +40% DR
Healing 4d8 HP, within 2 m 8d8 HP, within 4 m 12d8 HP, within 8 m 16d8 HP, within 16 m
Active Buff Empowerment +1 PL, +1 Round +2 PL, +2 Rounds +3 PL, +3 Rounds +4 PL, +4 Rounds
Special Negation +2 Special Negation +4 Special Negation +8 Special Negation +12 Special Negation

Damage Reduction / Special Negation. Round-based defensive bonuses expire at Round End. Special Negation reduces incoming eligible hostile numeric Special(X); if reduced to 0 or less, it is not applied.

Healing. During Preparation, pay the normal cumulative Stone cost for one Healing application. Trigger it later in the current Round at a legal action boundary, targeting yourself or one ally within the listed Range. You may also trigger it before incoming HP damage; heal first, then resolve the hit's damage. Triggering uses no additional Stones, Attack Action, or Reaction. Roll once, then expend the prepared application. Unused Healing expires at Round End; Stones remain spent. Apply the current-Bar cap and the positive-Healing exception for living Incapacitated or Stable creatures. Eligible Maximization may enhance the roll.

Active Buff Empowerment. Improve one Active Buff activated this Round by the listed effective Power Levels (up to its normal PL cap) and extra duration. The improved Buff keeps its own resulting duration; this does not add another maintained Buff. Multiple Empowerment sources do not stack unless expressly allowed.

Influence Stone Abilities

Stone Ability Rank 1 Rank 2 Rank 3 Rank 4
Not a Target 1 enemy within 8 m Up to 2 enemies within 16 m Up to 3 enemies within 24 m Up to 4 enemies within 32 m
Cleanse Cleanse(2) Cleanse(4) Cleanse(8) Cleanse(16)
Colorless Recovery Up to 2 Stones Up to 4 Stones Up to 8 Stones Up to 16 Stones
Enemy Evade Reduction -1 Evade -2 Evade -4 Evade -8 Evade

Not a Target. Choose the listed number of enemies in Range during Preparation. Each cannot target you with its next attack this Round, unless you are its only valid target. The restriction expires at Round End.

Cleanse. Apply the listed Cleanse(X) to one creature within 20 m, including yourself. Distribute it among eligible negative Specials on that creature; one activation never affects multiple creatures.

Colorless Recovery. Activate once per combat during Preparation; pay the normal 1 / 3 / 7 / 15 Stones, which become Exhausted, not Sealed. No Passive: Absorption is required. Choose up to the listed number of Ready or Exhausted Colorless Stones; unused selection capacity may be assigned to Stones gained later in this combat. Those selected Stones may participate in the existing shared MR-Stones-per-Round Recovery until combat ends. They are not recovered immediately. The Rank and selection limit cannot later increase, and this Ability cannot be activated or stacked again in the same combat. Unselected Colorless Stones remain ineligible for normal Recovery. This creates no Stones, grants no additional Recovery, and never extends a Stone's own expiration. The activation Stones may recover normally if eligible, but this does not grant another use.

Enemy Evade Reduction. For your own attacks this Round, treat each targeted enemy as having the listed Evade penalty. Its actual Evade is unchanged, so allies gain no benefit. This is not Expose(X) and applies no Special.

Wits Stone Abilities

Stone Ability Rank 1 Rank 2 Rank 3 Rank 4
Phasing 1 Charge 2 Charges 3 Charges 4 Charges
Initiative Boost +1 x MR Initiative +2 x MR Initiative +4 x MR Initiative +8 x MR Initiative
Reaction Denial Deny 1 Reaction Deny 2 Reactions Deny 3 Reactions Deny 4 Reactions
Movement Reduction Halve Movement of 1 enemy Halve Movement of 2 enemies Halve Movement of 3 enemies Halve Movement of 4 enemies

Phasing. Activate once per combat, regardless of Rank or source. Charges remain available until spent or combat ends.

Initiative Boost. Activate once per combat during the Preparation Phase's Initiative Exchange sequence. Add the bonus before Initiative is converted into Initiative Colorless Stones. Spent Stones become Exhausted normally.

Reaction Denial. Choose one enemy during Preparation. Deny its next 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 eligible Reaction declarations this Round, regardless of Reaction type. A denied Reaction has no effect but does not consume the enemy's Reaction allowance. Each denied declaration uses one denial; the same Reaction cannot be re-declared against the same trigger.

Movement Reduction. Halve the distance of every individual Movement Action this Round for the selected enemies, including additional Movements. Round half-metres up (5 m to 3 m, 7 m to 4 m). This does not change base Speed, remove Movements, or apply twice to the same Movement. Resolve separate Slow reductions under their own rules.

::

Last Breath

Once per Safe Haven Rest, when you would drop to Incapacitated, you may burn 1 Stone from any Attribute. You remain conscious with 1 free box in your Wounded Health Bar. Any remaining damage from the triggering damage instance is ignored. You cannot use Last Breath again until you complete a Safe Haven Rest.

::

Types of Powers

Types of Powers

Powers are divided into five main types:

Power Type Short Description
Active Action-based Powers for attacks, healing, effects, zones, barriers, and Special delivery.
Passive Ongoing character features that define your baseline and combat identity.
Active Buff Temporary combat states, stances, auras, or short-term enhancements; mechanical size changes use Transformation, while Form is visual only.
Reaction Immediate responses to specific triggers outside your turn.
Movement Power Special movement options that replace your normal Movement.

For full rules, templates, pricing, limits, and examples, see the dedicated Power Catalogues. Only a qualifying damaging Instant Active Power with its own printed Damage Dice may be learned as a Limited Power; see Limited Power Modifier for uses per Safe Haven Rest and doubled Power Damage Dice. Special-only Powers are never Limited.

A Shared Combat Language

Destroyed Faith uses a shared mechanical language for combat. Many combat abilities are built from a limited set of standardized effects called Specials. Specials are not an additional layer of rules placed on top of your abilities. They are the building blocks from which many of those abilities are created.

Each Special has one clear mechanical function. Ruin deals damage. Slow reduces Movement. Corrode reduces Armor. Hex increases Spell Damage. Sundered does the same for non-Spell Damage, and so on. You do not need to memorize every Special before you play. Learn the ones your character uses. When another Special appears at the table, its effect can simply be looked up or explained once. Once you know a Special, you know what it does wherever it appears.

Different characters may describe the same Special in completely different ways. A curse, a weapon technique, an artifact, or a supernatural power may look entirely different in the fiction while using the same mechanical effect.

Characters normally specialize in only a small number of Specials and combine them with the abilities of the rest of the group. This creates tactical combinations without requiring every individual Power to introduce its own separate set of rules.

Specials are not additional systems to learn. They are the shared vocabulary from which much of combat is built.

::

Power Tags

Tag: Spell

Any Power that interacts with the Veil the boundary between matter and will gains the (Spell) tag.
Only abilities that explicitly reference “Spells” can target, dispel or suppress these effects.

Examples: Ruin, Root, Bless, Hex Bolt, Healing Pulse.

Progression (XP)

Progression (XP)

At the end of each session, the GM awards XP.

Record the same award in two places:

  • Lifetime Experience is the total XP your character has ever earned. It only increases and is never reduced by spending XP.
  • Banked XP is the spendable currency used for Attributes, Skills, Powers, Artifacts, Mastery Trees, and other GM-approved progression options.

You may bank XP and spend it later during downtime or another GM-approved Upgrade Step. Spending Banked XP never reduces Lifetime Experience.

Characters begin with 2 permanent Stones. Every 20 Lifetime XP unlocks 1 additional permanent Stone at the next Upgrade Step. This Stone progression is automatic and does not depend on how the character spends XP.

XP Reward by Mastery Rank

Mastery Rank Recommended XP / Session
MR 1–2 4–6 XP
MR 3 6–8 XP
MR 4 8–10 XP
MR 5 10–12 XP
MR 6+ 12–14 XP

The GM chooses the exact XP reward based on session impact, danger, progress, roleplay, discovery, and story relevance. For standard group play, award the same session XP to all player characters so Lifetime Experience, permanent Stone progression, and Mastery Rank remain synchronized.

A quiet session, travel session, investigation-heavy session, or mostly social session may grant the lower value.
A dangerous session, major victory, important discovery, boss fight, or story milestone may grant the higher value.

Upgrade Steps

XP is spent during an Upgrade Step.

An Upgrade Step usually happens during downtime, after a session, during a Safe Haven Rest, or whenever the GM allows character progression.

During each Upgrade Step, each individual upgrade may be increased only once.

This means:

  • You may increase several different Attributes.
  • You may increase several different Skills.
  • You may increase several different Powers.
  • You may increase several different Artifacts.
  • You may not increase the same Attribute twice in the same Upgrade Step.
  • You may not increase the same Skill twice in the same Upgrade Step.
  • You may not increase the same Power twice in the same Upgrade Step.
  • You may not increase the same Artifact twice in the same Upgrade Step.

This rule replaces the old Attribute 50% spending limit.

There is no longer a fixed percentage limit on Attribute spending.
Instead, spendable progression is controlled by the Upgrade Step limit and XP costs. Stone progression is separate and follows Lifetime Experience automatically.

Example: Legal Upgrade Step

A character spends XP during downtime.

They may choose:

  • Might +1
  • Agility +1
  • Athletics +1
  • Survival +1
  • Main Attack Power +1 Level
  • Armor Artifact +1 Level

This is legal because each individual value was increased only once.

Example: Illegal Upgrade Step

A character cannot spend XP to do this in one Upgrade Step:

  • Might +1
  • Might +1 again
  • Might +1 again

Even if the character has enough banked XP, the same individual Attribute cannot be increased more than once in the same Upgrade Step.

The player may save XP and increase Might again in a later Upgrade Step.

Attribute and Skill Costs

Attributes use the compressed 1–40 scale; Skills retain their existing 1–32 progression. Use the new value reached to determine the cost of a +1 increase.

New Value Attribute Cost / +1 Skill Cost / +1
1–4 2 XP 1 XP
5–8 4 XP 1 XP
9–12 6 XP 2 XP
13–16 8 XP 2 XP
17–20 10 XP 3 XP
21–24 12 XP 3 XP
25–28 14 XP 4 XP
29–32 16 XP 4 XP
33–36 18 XP —
37–40 20 XP —

The compressed Attribute costs preserve the long-term XP cost of the former wider scale while making each individual Attribute increase more meaningful. Skills remain cheaper and keep their normal maximum of 32.

For example, Skill 8→9 costs 2 XP; Attribute 7→8 costs 4 XP; Attribute 8→9 costs 6 XP.

Attribute Cap

No Attribute can normally exceed 40. The cap limits dice-pool growth only; it does not determine Stone assignment. Stones follow Lifetime Experience and the Mastery Rank × 2 per-Attribute concentration limit.

Lifetime Experience & Stone Progression

Stones are not purchased and are not generated by Attribute thresholds. Every character begins with 2 permanent Stones and gains 1 additional permanent Stone every 20 Lifetime XP. Spending XP never lowers Lifetime Experience or removes earned progression. At an Upgrade Step, assign any unassigned permanent Stones earned after the 2 starting Attribute Stones to Attributes, up to MR × 2 Stones per Attribute. Instead, each such Stone may be chosen as 1 Permanent Colorless Stone at a 1:1 ratio. There is no additional Stone cost and no MR cap on Permanent Colorless Stones. They are not assigned to an Attribute and do not count against Attribute Stone limits; however, only Attribute Stones unlock Attribute Stone Abilities.

Stone progression and Mastery Rank progression both use Lifetime XP, but they are separate tracks:

  • every 20 Lifetime XP grants 1 permanent Stone,
  • specific Lifetime XP milestones increase Mastery Rank,
  • spending Banked XP changes neither track.

Core Lifetime XP Milestones

Lifetime XP Permanent Stones Earned Mastery Rank
0 / Start 2 MR2
100 7 MR3
200 12 MR4
400 22 MR5
600 32 MR6
800 42 MR7
1000 52 MR8

Between these milestones, continue gaining one permanent Stone every 20 Lifetime XP normally. The character sheet should display at least the first 1000 Lifetime XP of the progression track, with visible Stone ticks every 20 XP and Mastery Rank milestones at 100 / 200 / 400 / 600 / 800 / 1000 XP. A full divine progression track may continue to 2200 Lifetime XP.

MR 1–8 allow 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 / 12 / 14 / 16 assigned Stones per Attribute. Permanent Colorless Stones have no separate MR cap; only permanent Stones earned after the 2 starting Attribute Stones may be chosen as Colorless.

At 2200 Lifetime XP, the normal permanent Stone progression reaches 112 earned permanent Stones. This is the normal system progression ceiling; no additional permanent Stones are earned beyond that point unless a rule explicitly extends divine progression.

Initiative Colorless Stones and other source-granted temporary Stones never increase Lifetime XP, never grant permanent Stone progression, and never affect Mastery Rank.

Power Costs

Power Level cost equals twice the new Power Level.

New Power Level XP Cost
1 2 XP
2 4 XP
3 6 XP
4 8 XP
5 10 XP
6 12 XP
7 14 XP
8 16 XP
9 18 XP
10 20 XP
11 22 XP
12 24 XP
13 26 XP
14 28 XP
15 30 XP
16 32 XP

A Power may only be increased by one Level during the same Upgrade Step.

Power Level Cap by Mastery Rank

Mastery Rank Maximum Power Level
MR 1 Level 2
MR 2 Level 4
MR 3 Level 6

Mastery Rank Progression

Mastery Rank Progression

Mastery Rank reflects how far a character has progressed through their lifetime journey and how much power they can safely express, sustain, and control.

You normally begin at Mastery Rank 2, representing a trained adventurer or awakened Spark.

For standard player progression, Lifetime Experience directly determines Mastery Rank. Mastery Rank is not purchased, is not calculated from assigned Stones, and is not reduced when XP is spent.

Mastery Progression

Lifetime XP Mastery Rank Tier Description
0–99 MR2 – Adept Awakened mortal; trained adventurer.
100–199 MR3 – Expert Seasoned Spark; tactical combat options become reliable.
200–399 MR4 – Master Hero-tier; multiple systems begin to work together.
400–599 MR5 – Grandmaster Epic champion; exceptional mortal or supernatural elite.
600–799 MR6 – Legend Demon Prince ceiling; world-threatening legendary beings.
800–999 MR7 – Mythic Titans, demigods, archangels, divine remnants, and ancient horrors.
1000+ MR8 – God True gods and cosmic entities. This is the highest possible Mastery Rank.

Divine Scale within MR8

MR8 covers a wide divine range. Two beings may both be MR8 while still standing at very different points on the divine scale.

Lifetime XP Divine Scale
1000–1199 Lesser God
1200–1399 True God
1400–1599 High God
1600–2199 Apex God
2200+ System Limit

MR8 is not expected as normal campaign progression. It represents gods, cosmic beings, final ascensions, or campaign-ending transformations. At 2200 Lifetime XP, normal permanent Stone progression has reached its system ceiling of 112 earned permanent Stones unless an explicit rule extends it.

Shared Mastery Recommendation

For a balanced campaign, all player characters should usually share the same Mastery Rank.

Characters with the same Lifetime XP may distribute their permanent Stones very differently across Attributes or convert some progression into Permanent Colorless Stones. They may also have different Attributes, Skills, Powers, and Artifacts. Their Mastery Rank nevertheless remains synchronized as long as they receive the same Lifetime XP awards.

A GM may still set a different starting Mastery Rank or use exceptional story-based advancement for special campaigns, NPCs, transformations, or divine ascension, but this is an explicit exception rather than the normal progression rule.

Mastery Rank Effects

Each time your Mastery Rank increases, you gain:

  • access to the next Mastery Rank tier,
  • increased Keep according to the core dice rules,
  • stronger MR-based durations and uses,
  • improved Stone recovery where applicable,
  • access to higher Power Level caps,
  • increased per-Attribute Stone concentration (Permanent Colorless Stones have no MR-based cap).

Mastery Rank is not only a number. It defines how much power a character can safely express, sustain, and control.

Session count depends on the XP awarded at the table. The progression itself does not depend on whether a player spends Banked XP on Attributes, Skills, Powers, Artifacts, or other options.

MR7 remains mythic play. MR8 remains godlevel. The normal permanent Stone progression ceiling is reached at 2200 Lifetime XP.

Design Note: Two Independent Progression Axes

The Mastery System separates what you buy from how far you have traveled.

Banked XP is player choice. Spend it on Attributes, Skills, Powers, Artifacts, Mastery Trees, utility, or character-specific options. No category must be purchased merely to keep pace with Stone progression.

Lifetime Experience is the long-term progression axis. It unlocks Stone progression automatically every 20 XP earned and increases Mastery Rank at the fixed Lifetime XP milestones, regardless of how Banked XP is spent.

This separation is intentional. A character may keep an Attribute low, invest heavily in Skills, or focus on Powers and Artifacts without being punished by losing access to Stones. Likewise, a character may raise Attributes aggressively for larger dice Pools without automatically gaining more supernatural affinity.

MR6 represents the upper limit of demon-level beings. MR7 represents entities such as Titans, demigods, archangels, and divine remnants. MR8 represents true gods.
